tagline: South Africa's Mother City pairs the flat top of Table Mountain with beaches, penguins, world-class wine country and the Cape of Good Hope. It is ranked #6 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Cape Town was founded in 1652 as a supply station for Dutch ships sailing to the East Indies, making it South Africa's oldest city. Its mix of African, Dutch, British and Malay heritage shows up everywhere, from the colorful houses of Bo-Kaap to Cape Malay cuisine.

Table Mountain rises more than 1,000 metres above the city. A rotating cable car reaches the top in minutes, while hikers climb routes like Platteklip Gorge. Below, the V&A Waterfront mixes shops, restaurants and harbour views, and ferries leave for Robben Island, where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 18 years.

The surroundings are just as famous. Boulders Beach is home to a colony of African penguins, the Cape of Good Hope marks the dramatic southwestern tip of the continent, and the Constantia and Stellenbosch wine regions are a short drive away.

funFacts.title: THE MOTHER CITY
funFacts.text: Locals call Cape Town the 'Mother City', a nickname linked to its status as South Africa's first European settlement.

funFacts.title: A FLAT-TOPPED MOUNTAIN
funFacts.text: Table Mountain's plateau stretches about 3 kilometres, and its 'tablecloth' of cloud is caused by a famous local wind.

funFacts.title: PENGUINS ON THE BEACH
funFacts.text: A colony of African penguins has lived at Boulders Beach since 1982.

funFacts.title: SOUTH AFRICA'S OLDEST CITY
funFacts.text: Founded in 1652, Cape Town predates every other major city in the country.

funFacts.title: TWO OCEANS NEARBY
funFacts.text: The Atlantic and Indian Oceans meet near Cape Agulhas, southeast of the city, at one of the world's famous maritime crossroads.

funFacts.title: ROBBEN ISLAND
funFacts.text: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in prison on Robben Island, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

funFacts.title: A NEW WONDER OF NATURE
funFacts.text: Table Mountain was voted one of the New7Wonders of Nature in 2011.

funFacts.title: THE COLORFUL BO-KAAP
funFacts.text: Bo-Kaap's bright houses were historically home to Cape Malay residents, and the area is known for its cuisine and culture.

funFacts.title: A MEDICAL FIRST
funFacts.text: The world's first human heart transplant was performed at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town in 1967.

funFacts.title: A FLORAL KINGDOM
funFacts.text: The Cape Floral Region is the smallest and, for its size, richest of the world's six floral kingdoms.
